items.title: Section: The Four Bases of Power Close in Full

items.zh: 由二因緣，於隨眠斷分別了知。謂由境界不現見思，及由境界現見捨故。如是名為八種斷行，亦名勝行。如是八種斷行、勝行，即是為害隨眠瑜伽。此中欲者，即是彼欲；此中策勵，即彼精進；此中信者，即是彼信；此中安、念、正知、思、捨，即彼方便。如是此中，若先欲等四三摩地，若今所說八種斷行，於為永斷所有隨眠圓滿成辨三摩地時，一切總名欲三摩地斷行成就神足、勤三摩地斷行成就神足、心三摩地斷行成就神足、觀三摩地斷行成就神足。問：
items.en: Through two conditions, one clearly discerns whether the latent seeds have been cut off: through thinking about an object not directly seen, and through equanimity towards an object directly seen. This is called the eight kinds of conditioning, also called the excellent practices. These eight kinds of conditioning, or excellent practices, are precisely the yogic discipline for destroying the latent seeds. Here, aspiration is that same aspiration named earlier; here, self-spurring is that same diligence; here, faith is that same faith; and here, pliancy, mindfulness, clear comprehension, volition, and equanimity are that same means. Thus, both the four concentrations explained earlier and the eight kinds of conditioning explained now, taken together, at the point of permanently cutting off every latent seed and bringing concentration to full completion, are together called the basis of power through aspiration-concentration and conditioning, the basis of power through effort-concentration and conditioning, the basis of power through mind-concentration and conditioning, and the basis of power through investigation-concentration and conditioning.

items.title: Section: Why "Bases of Power" — Two Explanations, Worldly and Supramundane

items.zh: 何因緣故說名神足？答：如有足者，能往能還，騰躍勇健，能得能證世間所有殊勝之法。世殊勝法說名為神，彼能到此，故名神足。如是若有如是諸法，有三摩地圓滿成辨，彼心如是清淨鮮白，無諸瑕穢，離隨煩惱，安住正直，有所堪能，獲得不動，能往能還，騰躍勇健，能得能證出世間法。由出世法最勝自在，是最勝神，彼能證此，故名神足。
items.en: What is the reason it is called the basis of power? Answer: just as one who has feet can go out and return, leaping vigorously, able to reach and realise all the excellent states the world has to offer — worldly excellence is here called "power," and that which arrives there is called its "basis." Likewise, when these very factors bring concentration to full completion, the mind becomes pure and bright, free of every blemish, free of the secondary afflictions, settled in uprightness, genuinely capable, having attained the unshakeable — able to go out and return, leaping vigorously, able to reach and realise supramundane states. Since the supramundane teaching is the most excellent and free of all, it is called the "greatest power," and that which realises it is called its "basis."

items.title: The Five Faculties Open: Faith Generating Everything Beyond It

items.zh: 彼由如是勝三摩地為所依持，勝三摩地為所依止，能進修習增上心學、增上慧學所有瑜伽。由進修習此瑜伽故，於他大師、弟子所證，深生勝解、深生淨信。此清淨信增上義故，說名信根。問：於何增上？答：於能生起出世間法而為上首，及於能起精進、念、定、慧為其增上。餘精進等，於能生起出世間法，及於能起展轉乃至慧為其增上。乃至其慧，唯於能起出世間法為其增上。是故信等說名五根。
items.en: Resting on such excellent concentration as its support, the practitioner is able to advance in cultivating all yogic practice belonging to higher mind-training and higher wisdom-training. Through advancing in this cultivation, one generates deep confidence and deep pure faith in what the Teacher and his disciples have realised. Because this pure faith has the meaning of increasing further excellence, it is called the faculty of faith. It is the head, generating the supramundane teaching, and also increases diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. The remaining faculties — diligence and the rest — likewise generate the supramundane teaching, and successively increase one another up through wisdom. Wisdom, finally, only generates the supramundane teaching itself. This is why faith and the rest are called the five faculties.

items.title: The Five Powers: Faith Unshakeable by Any Force

items.zh: 若復了知前後所證而有差別，隨此能於後後所證出世間法，深生勝解、深生淨信。此清淨信難伏義故，說名信力。問：誰不能伏？答：此清淨信，若天、若魔、若諸沙門、若婆羅門、若餘世間，無有如法能引奪者，諸煩惱纏亦不能屈，故名難伏。此為上首、此為前行，餘精進等亦名為力。由此諸力具大威勢，摧伏一切魔軍勢力，能證一切諸漏永盡，是故名力。
items.en: Further knowing the difference between what has already been realised and what comes progressively after, and, in accordance with this, generating deep confidence and deep pure faith regarding the successively higher supramundane teachings to be realised — because this pure faith has the meaning of being difficult to subdue, it is called the power of faith. Question: subdued by whom? Answer: this pure faith cannot be legitimately taken away by any god, any demon, any ascetic, any brahmin, or anyone else in the world whatsoever — nor can it be overcome even by one's own remaining afflictions. This is why it is called difficult to subdue. Because these powers possess such great and majestic force, able to overcome the entire host of Māra's armies and to realise the complete and permanent exhaustion of every defilement, they are therefore called powers.

items.title: Faith's Faculty and Power as Cause of the Four Confirmed Purities

items.zh: 當觀此中信根、信力，即四證淨中所有淨信。何以故？以其證入正性離生所有證淨，皆由此因、此緣、此序，由彼即是此增上果。是故世尊就其因果相屬道理，說言當觀即彼證淨，非即彼體、非即彼相。
items.en: One should observe that the faculty and power of faith here are precisely the pure faith found within the four confirmed purities. This is because the confirmed purity attained upon entering the true nature that departs from arising all comes about through this very cause, this very condition, this very inception — that confirmed purity is simply this faith's own increased result. This is why the Bhagavān, in terms of how cause and result belong to one another, said one should regard the two as the same confirmed purity — though not identical in essence, nor identical in characteristic.

items.title: Section: The Remaining Four Faculties and Powers Close in Full

items.zh: 當觀此中精進根、力，即四正斷中所有精進。此何正斷？謂能永斷見道所斷一切煩惱方便正斷，此中意說如是正斷。由此正斷，畢竟能斷所有諸惡不善法故。當觀此中念根、念力，即四念住中所有正念。謂四念住能無餘斷一切顛倒。當觀此中定根、定力，即四靜慮中所有正定。謂諸靜慮能為方便，證不還果。當觀此中慧根、慧力，即四聖諦中所有正智。謂聖諦智於四聖諦能證現觀，得沙門果。
items.en: One should observe that the faculty and power of diligence here are precisely the diligence found within the four right efforts — namely, the preparatory correct cutting capable of permanently ending every affliction abandoned at the path of seeing. One should observe that the faculty and power of mindfulness here are precisely the correct mindfulness found within the four foundations — the four foundations being capable of ending every distorted view without remainder. One should observe that the faculty and power of concentration here are precisely the correct concentration found within the four absorptions — the absorptions serving as the means to realise the fruit of non-returning. One should observe that the faculty and power of wisdom here are precisely the correct knowledge found within the four noble truths — the truth-knowledge capable of realising direct insight into the four truths and attaining the fruit of a renunciant.

blocks.text: Why the bases of power are so named, then the five faculties and five powers.

"Through two conditions one discerns whether the latent seeds have been cut: thinking about an object not present, and equanimity towards an object present." If affliction still stirs, the seeds remain.

"Just as one who has feet can go out and return, leaping vigorously, able to reach all excellent states", so these concentrations are the feet of spiritual power. "Worldly excellence is called power; what arrives there is its basis." With them, "the mind becomes pure and bright, free of every blemish".

Faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom, each "generating what comes after it". "Because pure faith has the meaning of increasing further excellence, it is called the faculty of faith." Master Cháng Bǎi: nothing follows wisdom; wisdom is the last.
The same five, now "difficult to subdue": faith that "no god, demon, ascetic, or brahmin can shake". Venerable Miào Jìng: the god is Brahmā, the demon Māra.

The faculty and power of faith are the faith in the four confirmed purities; of effort, the four right efforts; of mindfulness, the four foundations; of concentration, the absorptions; of wisdom, the knowledge of the four truths.

quiz.q: By what two conditions does one discern whether the seeds are cut, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng divide volition and equanimity?
options: thinking about unseen objects, equanimity towards seen ones
quiz.why: "Through two conditions, one clearly discerns whether the latent seeds have been cut off: through thinking about an object not directly seen, and through equanimity towards an object directly seen." Venerable Miào Jìng: here "not directly seen" is volition, "directly seen" is equanimity.

quiz.q: "Worldly excellence is called 'power.'" What does Master Cháng Bǎi say worldly excellence is?
quiz.why: "Worldly excellence is here called 'power,' and that which arrives there is called its 'basis.'" Master Cháng Bǎi: the excellent states of the world are superhuman states — absorption; absorption is called "power."

quiz.q: The supramundane basis of power is "free of the secondary afflictions, settled in uprightness." What problem does Venerable Miào Jìng say one with absorption may have?
options: though accomplished in absorption, has craving, views, and great pride
quiz.why: "The mind becomes pure and bright, free of every blemish, free of the secondary afflictions, settled in uprightness." Venerable Miào Jìng: some accomplish absorption yet have craving, views, and pride — very high pride. Hence the supramundane basis must be free of secondary afflictions.

quiz.q: Why is it called the faculty of faith, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say follows from faith?
options: pure faith has the sense of increasing; faith leads to vow, vow to practise, practice to supramundane good
quiz.why: "Because this pure faith has the meaning of increasing further excellence, it is called the faculty of faith." Venerable Miào Jìng: with faith comes vow, with vow comes practice, and with practice supramundane wholesome states arise.

quiz.q: Why does the wisdom faculty "only generate the supramundane"? What do the masters say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: nothing comes after it — prajñā is highest; Miào Jìng: it is still worldly wisdom but able to give rise to the supramundane
quiz.why: "Wisdom, finally, only generates the supramundane teaching itself." Master Cháng Bǎi: nothing follows wisdom; prajñā is the highest in the world, so no further mutual increase is mentioned. Venerable Miào Jìng: this wisdom is still worldly, but it has the capacity to give rise to the supramundane.

quiz.q: The power of faith is "difficult to subdue." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: even if the Buddha told him not to go forth, he would not listen
quiz.why: "Because this pure faith has the meaning of being difficult to subdue, it is called the power of faith." Master Cháng Bǎi: even if the Buddha came and told him not to go forth, he would not listen — that is how far it has gone.

quiz.q: Wisdom is truth-knowledge "realising direct insight." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain direct insight?
options: not inferring the truths but truly experiencing the emptiness of self
quiz.why: "The truth-knowledge capable of realising direct insight into the four truths and attaining the fruit of a renunciant." Master Cháng Bǎi: truth-knowledge does not know the four truths by inference; it is the mind truly experiencing the emptiness of self.
